item.description: En 2024, Chile vivió uno de los incendios más mortíferos de su historia, con 138 fallecidos y más de 14.000 viviendas destruidas en la región de Valparaíso. Ahora, siete personas fueron declaradas culpables por provocar deliberadamente el fuego, entre ellas exbomberos y brigadistas forestales. La Fiscalía busca que reciban cadena perpetua por su presunta responsabilidad en una tragedia que conmocionó al país. Mientras se espera la sentencia, Chile se prepara para una nueva temporada de incendios marcada por altas temperaturas. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: A North Carolina family donated the development rights over their 55-acre farm straddling two counties, protecting pasture and forest in a fast-growing region where most of the soil is considered prime farmland.
item.description: In North Carolina, Jennifer and Lane Tredway donated development rights to protect their 55-acre farm. This conservation easement will ensure the land remains agricultural and untouched by future development. The farm, known as Two Paths Farm, is situated in an area experiencing rapid urban expansion. Both Johnston and Wake counties are involved in preserving the agricultural character of the region. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: After 2015 divorce, Ohio court sets ex-husband’s share of Colorado home expenses at $101,723
item.description: In a recent ruling, the Ohio Court of Appeals reversed a lower court decision regarding property expenses. The court found that the husband had failed to pay various property-related costs, which resulted in a significant debt. The appellate court ordered him to reimburse his ex-wife a total of $101,723.27. This amount included unpaid taxes, insurance, and maintenance expenses related to their jointly held property. item.title: West Virginia town sues to save 12 historic buildings from demolition in national park
item.description: Thurmond, a historic railroad town in West Virginia, is in a legal battle against the National Park Service. The lawsuit aims to halt the planned demolition of 12 historic buildings scheduled for November 30. Officials argue the agency violated federal laws and failed to consider preservation options. Concerns have also been raised regarding road safety and equipment weight limits. The court's decision will determine the future of these historic structures. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Senegal regain AFCON title on appeal at Morocco's expense
item.description: Senegal on Tuesday regained their Africa Cup of Nations title after winning an appeal at the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the decision by the Confederation of African Football to declare Morocco the winners following a chaotic final in January. CAS said in a statement it had "upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF)" by a "unanimous decision". item.title: Life expectancy in Cuba falls for first time since 1950 amid economic crisis
item.description: WHO chief says life expectancy has fallen from 78.8 years in 2020 to 74.4 in 2025, figures that predate US fuel blockade Life expectancy has fallen for the first time in Cuba since 1950 as the island reels from a severe economic crisis, the head of the World Health Organization (WHO) said on Tuesday. On a visit to Havana, WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said life expectancy had fallen from 78.8 years in 2020 to 74.4 years in 2025, the first decline since records began in 1950. item.title: A Texas cliff has yielded evidence that Indigenous communities drove bison over its edge repeatedly
item.description: Recent archaeological discoveries have uncovered that Indigenous peoples utilized cliffs as bison jumps for millennia. The Nighthawk site in Texas showcases bison remains from various hunting events, demonstrating the importance of these communal hunts in shaping social and political dynamics within communities. Evidence also indicates that hunters revisited this site across generations, refining their tools and strategies, challenging previous assumptions about bison hunting in the Southern Plains. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
